topic: How a Bill becomes an Act
question: Explain the stages through which an ordinary Bill passes in Parliament before it becomes an Act.
sources: Constitution of India, Article 107 (introduction and passing of Bills), Article 108 (joint sitting) and Article 111 (assent to Bills)

points.label: Introduction (first reading)
points.description: An ordinary Bill may be introduced in either House of Parliament by a minister or a private member; the motion for leave to introduce is passed and the Bill is published.

points.label: Second reading and committee stage
points.description: The House discusses the general principles of the Bill and may send it to a select or joint committee; the Bill is then considered clause by clause and amendments are moved and voted on.
points.basis: Constitution of India, Article 107 and the rules of procedure of each House

points.label: Third reading
points.description: The House debates the Bill as a whole and votes to accept or reject it; only formal changes are allowed at this stage.
points.basis: Rules of procedure of each House of Parliament

points.label: Bill in the other House
points.description: The passed Bill goes to the other House, which goes through the same stages; if the Houses disagree, the President may call a joint sitting to settle the deadlock.

points.label: President's assent
points.description: After both Houses pass it, the Bill goes to the President, who may give assent, withhold assent, or return it once for reconsideration; once assent is given the Bill becomes an Act.
